Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Supply Installation Testing Commissioning of Goods and Training of operators and providing Statutory Clearances required (if any) 3. Service & Support Availability of Service Centres: Bidder/OEM must have a Functional Service Centre in the State of each Consignee's Location in case of carry-in warranty. (Not applicable in case of goods having on-site warranty). If service center is not already there at the time of bidding, successful bidder / OEM shall have to establish one within 30 days of award of contract. Payment shall be released only after submission of documentary evidence of having Functional Service Centre. 4. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 5. Service & Support Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 6. Warranty Bidder / OEM has to give an undertaking that after expiry of warranty period, it will provide Comprehensive Maintenance Service for next 5 years for the offered products at the rate not more than 5 % of contract price per annum. Buyer reserves the right to enter into a CMC agreement with the Successful Bidder / OEM after expiry of the Warranty period at above mentioned rate and the payment for the CMC charges would be made Quarterly after rendering of the CMC Services of the relevant CMC period. Performance Security of the successful bidder shall be forfeited if it fails to accept the CMC contract when called upon by the buyer. CMC would include cost of All required spare parts (Upload the undertaking). The original Performance Security of contract will be returned only after submission and verification of AMC Performance Security for 10% of total CMC value valid up to CMC period plus 2 months (if there is no other claim). 7. Warranty

Warranty period of the supplied products shall be 5 years from the date of final acceptance of goods or after completion of installation, commissioning & testing of goods (if included in the scope of supply), at consignee location. OEM Warranty certificates must be submitted by Successful Bidder at the time of delivery of Goods. The seller should guarantee the rectification of goods in case of any break down during the guarantee period. Seller should have well established Installation, Commissioning, Training, Troubleshooting and Maintenance Service group in INDIA for attending the after sales service. Details of Service Centres near consignee destinations are to be uploaded along with the bid. 8. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 1. The L1 firm will have to sign the Integrity pack in due course of time. 4. The experience should be continuous of 03 years OR 03 out of 05 years alongwith Crack/Installation/workin g satisfactory report. 5. Only representations/correspondence submitted via GeM shall be accepted. Any external representations/ correspondence made outside GeM shall not be accepted.

6. Equipment should be quoted as per the specification attached at ATC.. 7. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS 1. The analyzer should be a battery-operated/electrically powered, handh eld, cartridge-based, point-of-care blood gas analyzer for quantitative i n-vitro measurement of blood pH, pCO2, pO2, electrolytes along with c alculation of derived parameters, for bedside clinical decision-making i n sick and preterm neonates, including ELBW/VLBW infants. 2. The analyzer should be battery operated with a docking/charging stati on. 3. Essential measured parameters: 1. pH – Hydrogen ion concentration / acid–base status 2. pCO₂ – Partial pressure of carbon dioxide 3. pO₂ – Partial pressure of oxygen 4. Na⁺ – Sodium ion concentration 5. K⁺ – Potassium ion concentration 6. Cl⁻ – Chloride ion concentration ionized calcium (iCa++) 7. Glucose 8. Lactate 9. Haematocrit/haemoglobin (derived or measured) 4. Essential Calculated parameters: 1. Bicarbonate (HCO3-) 2. Standard bicarbonate (SBC) 3. Anion gap 4. Base excess (BE) 5. Oxygen saturation (SaO2) 6. Alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient (A-aDO2) with a/A ratio 5. The analyzer should require a sample volume of ≤200 µl per full panel .

6. The analyzer should accept capillary, arterial, and venous whole blood samples. 7. The analyzer should provide results within ≤5 minutes per full sample run, from sample application to result display. 8. The analyzer should have fully automatic, cartridge-integrated/internal calibration for every test; no manual calibration gas cylinder handling or separate calibration step should be required at bedside. 9. The analyzer should have automatic internal quality control with every cartridge/test, with QC results and trend data viewable on-screen and/ or downloadable. 10. The analyzer should have: 1. LCD/graphic touchscreen or keypad-driven display 2. an inbuilt or docking-station printer for bedside result slips 3. patient ID entry capability 4. automatic data archiving for a given patient ID entry at least the las t 50 tests 5. data back-up provision for atleast 100 last tests run on machine. 6. Capability to transfer patient data to LIS/HIS is desirable. 11. The user interface should be in English, with a simple icon-based/step- by-step workflow. 12. The analyzer should have a noise level of less than 60 dB. 13. The charging station should operate on 220 V AC ±10%, 50 Hz, with surge protection. 14. The analyzer should have an integral rechargeable battery permitting untethered handheld operation, with a 30-60 minutes of continuous op eration on a full charge; the bidder should specify the exact number of tests/duration of continuous use per full charge. 15. The analyzer should operate continuously in an ambient temperature of 20–30°C and relative humidity of up to 90%.

16. External surfaces should be compatible with disinfection with alcohol o r chlorine-based wipes. 17. Used cartridges should be compatible with standard biomedical waste segregation and disposal protocols. 18. The analyzer should be CDSCO approved/hold a valid Medical Device L icence under the Medical Device Rules, 2017 (as amended); the manuf acturing facility should be ISO 13485 certified; the device should comp ly with IEC 60601-1 for electrical safety. US FDA/European CE certificat ion is acceptable in case of non-availability of BIS standards for this de vice category. 08 ALARM CONDITIONS 1. Should have a QC failure lock-out indicator. 2. Should have an insufficient sample volume/sample error indicator. 3. Should have a cartridge/reagent expired or invalid indicator. 4. Should have a low battery/power failure indicator. 5. Should have a system/device fault indicator. 09 TERMS AND CONDITIONS 1. Prices so quoted should be frozen for 10 years including warranty. 2. Warranty period: 5 years. 3. CAMC for 5 years after warranty. CAMC should cover preventive maint enance, service visits, labour and covered replacement parts/spares, e xcluding routine consumables. Items covered under CAMC and warrant y should be clearly enlisted, along with items not covered under CAMC and warranty. 4. Original literature, and not the photocopy, should be supplied with the quotation.

5. Company should certify that the model quoted is the latest and not ob solete, and spares are available for minimum 10 years including warra nty. Frozen rate should not be more than the price of the quoted rate o n the date of purchase. 6. Rate list of all the accessories/consumables should be provided separa tely. These rates should be frozen for next 10 years. 7. Physical demonstration of the quoted model will be taken to verify the specifications. 8. The supplier/company should install and commission the equipment, p erform safety and operation checks before handover, and provide han ds-on training to designated users. 9. The equipment should maintain minimum 98% uptime during warrant y/CAMC period. 10. Authorized service personnel should visit the consignee site as per CA MC clause. 11. The calibration procedure should be simple and user-friendly. The sup plier should provide the list of equipment/procedures required for local calibration and routine maintenance. 12. The bidder should submit all applicable certifications, licences and test reports with the technical bid and/or at the time of supply, as required. Certificates should correspond to the quoted model. 13. The above specifications are generic and performance-based and are n ot tailor-made for any particular make or model. Multiple reputed man ufacturers meeting the stated requirements should be eligible for cons ideration. 10 CONSUMABLES AND ACCESSORIES 1. Cartridges/reagent strips sufficient for 500 tests should be supplied alo ng with the machine at the time of installation. 2. Cartridges/strips should cover all essential parameters and calculated parameters (as per Technical Specifications) in a single cartridge/strip, to minimize sample splitting.

3. Quality control material/cartridges for a minimum of 500 tests, or as p er manufacturer protocol, should be supplied. 4. Consumables should preferably have room-temperature storage stabili ty. 5. Bidder should separately quote the per-cartridge/strip rate and the tot al annual consumable (cartridges/reagent strips, inclusive of QC mater ial) cost for a projected NICU workload of approximately 20 tests/day ( ≈ 7,300 tests/year). 6. Bidder should specify the reagent/cartridge shelf life, including on-boar d (post-installation, in-use) shelf life and storage temperature range. 7. supplier should provide local/regional service support in India (Chandig arh/Punjab/tricity region preferred), with a toll-free helpline and a docu mented response time for breakdown calls. 8. Two hard-copy sets plus a soft copy of the operating, technical, and se rvice manuals should be supplied in English, along with machine diagr ams. 9. A list of spares/accessories/cartridges with part numbers and indicativ e cost, including the annual consumable cost, should be supplied. . 9.
